title: Imperative 4: Plural and Polite Forms (add -те)
titleRussian: Повелительное наклонение 4: формы множественного числа и вежливые (добавляем -те)
description: Add -те to the 2sg command to address two or more people OR one person politely (вы): читай → читайте, говори → говорите, готовь → готовьте. The suffix -й / -и / -ь does not change.
descriptionRussian: К форме 2-го лица единственного числа добавляется -те, чтобы обратиться к нескольким людям ИЛИ к одному человеку на «вы»: читай → читайте, говори → говорите, готовь → готовьте.
intro: The cheapest lesson in the book: one syllable added to what you already built. What makes it worth its own lesson is not the form but the social choice behind it. The same ending covers speaking to several people and speaking politely to one, so getting it wrong does not produce a grammatical error. It produces a rude one.
rules: Add -те to the 2sg command to make the plural or polite form: читай → читайте, говори → говорите, готовь → готовьте.
The -те does not change the -й / -и / -ь choice. Get the 2sg right, then just add -те.
Use the -те form for two or more people (plural) and for one person you address politely as вы.
Use the plain 2sg form (no -те) only for one person you call ты: a friend, child, or family.
examples: Дети, читайте сейчас. (Children, read now.) Plural address; vowel stem чита- → -йте.
Анна Ивановна, читайте, пожалуйста. (Anna Ivanovna, please read.) Polite singular (вы); same form.
Друзья, говорите медленно. (Friends, speak slowly.) Plural address; consonant stem → -ите.
Лена, готовьте обед, пожалуйста. (Lena, please make dinner.) Polite singular; consonant stem → -ьте.
Откройте окно, пожалуйста. (Open the window, please.) Polite singular; vowel stem → -йте.
Идите домой. (Go home.) Plural OR polite singular; consonant stem → -ите.

items.promptEnglish: Read this book! (to one friend, as ты; warm-up)
items.hint: One friend you call ты. Vowel stem чита- + which suffix?
items.explanation: Warm-up from Lesson 1: vowel stem чита- + й → читай (the 2sg form for ты). Today we add -те to make the plural / polite form читайте.

items.hint: Several children. Add -те to the 2sg form.
items.explanation: Дети means several children, so use the plural form: читай + те = читайте.

items.hint: Several friends. Take the 2sg говори and add -те.
items.explanation: Друзья means several friends, so use the plural form: the 2sg говори (consonant stem, suffix -и from Lesson 1) plus -те gives говорите.

items.promptEnglish: Lena, please make dinner! (polite, addressing her as вы)
items.hint: One person, but politely as вы (note пожалуйста). Add -те to the -ь form.
items.explanation: Lena is one person, but addressed politely as вы, so use the -те form: готовь + те = готовьте.

items.promptEnglish: Open the window, please! (polite, as вы)
items.hint: Polite request with пожалуйста. Vowel stem откро- → -йте.
items.explanation: The polite request (пожалуйста, вы) takes the -те form. The 2sg открой (vowel stem, suffix -й) plus -те gives откройте.

items.hint: Several people (ребята). Take the 2sg иди and add -те.
items.explanation: Ребята means several people, so use the plural form: the 2sg иди (consonant stem, suffix -и) plus -те gives идите.

blanks: Анна Ивановна, _____ медленно, пожалуйста. (Anna Ivanovna, please speak slowly.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Both use вы, so both add -те. Anna Ivanovna is one person addressed politely (вы) → говорите. Дети are several people → откройте.

errorCorrection.explanation: Maria Petrovna is addressed politely as вы (note пожалуйста), so add -те: слушайте. The plain слушай is the form for one person you call ты (a friend, child, or family), so it clashes with the respectful address.

The 2sg of писать is пиши (suffix -и, because пишу́ is end-stressed), so the plural just adds -те: пишите. The form пишьте wrongly uses -ь, which belongs to stem-stressed verbs like готовь → готовьте.
The 2sg of встать is встань (suffix -ь), so the plural adds -те: встаньте. The lookalike встанете is 'you will stand up' (a statement), not a command; watch the -ете vs -ьте trap.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Lena, please buy bread. (Lena is addressed politely, as вы)
errorCorrection.explanation: Lena is addressed politely as вы here, so add -те: купи + те = купите. The plain купи is the 2sg form for one person you call ты. The suffix -и does not change; you only add -те.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Anna Ivanovna, please open the window. (polite, as вы)
minimalPairs.explanation: Anna Ivanovna is addressed politely as вы (note пожалуйста), so add -те: откройте. Открой is the form for one person you call ты (a friend, child, or family), which does not fit a respectful request.
Дети means several children, so use the plural form идите. Иди is the form for one person addressed as ты.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Misha, clean your room. (one child you call ты)
minimalPairs.explanation: Misha is one child you call ты, so use the plain 2sg form убери, no -те. Уберите would be the plural / polite form for вы, which does not fit speaking to one child you know well.

sentenceBuilding.translation: Please open the window. (politely, to вы)

categorySorting.instruction: Sort each command by the form it uses. ты forms have no -те; вы forms add -те.

reviewVocab.definition: the ending added to a 2sg command to address several people, or one person politely as вы: читай → читайте, говори → говорите, готовь → готовьте
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Дети, читайте!' форма читайте — это 2sg читай плюс -те.

reviewVocab.definition: you (plural, or polite for one person); takes the -те form of the command
reviewVocab.example: Анна Ивановна, читайте, пожалуйста — вежливое обращение к одному человеку на вы.

reviewVocab.definition: you (one person you know well: a friend, child, or family); takes the plain command with no -те
reviewVocab.example: Лена, читай — обращение к одному близкому человеку на ты, без -те.
